panels.title: Executors: Busy vs Total
panels.description: Dynamic agent Pods only (see jenkins/jcasc/jenkins.yaml Kubernetes cloud) - a sustained gap between these two lines usually means agent Pods are failing to schedule (RBAC, node capacity, or image pull), not that Jenkins itself is unhealthy.

panels.title: Build Outcomes, All Jobs (rate, 1h window)
panels.description: jenkins_runs_{success,failure}_total are global counters (not per-job) as exposed by this project's pinned Prometheus plugin version - confirmed against a real controller. See the per-job health-score panel for job-level breakdown instead.

panels.title: Last Build Duration by Job
panels.description: Per-job breakdown requires JCasC's prometheusConfiguration.perBuildMetrics: true (see jenkins/jcasc/jenkins.yaml) - without it, every default_jenkins_builds_* metric carries no jenkins_job label at all (also confirmed live).

panels.title: Per-Job Health Score
panels.description: Jenkins's own built-in 0-100 health score per job (recent build stability) - "is the supply chain healthy, and is anything blocking it?" answered per-job rather than only in aggregate.

panels.title: Time Since Last Successful cd-application Run
panels.description: The final project's own worked example: from this panel you can tell whether the last GREEN deploy was minutes or days ago, without opening Jenkins at all. Empty/no-data until cd-application has completed at least one successful build.

panels.title: Controller JVM Heap Usage
panels.description: The controller never runs a build itself (numExecutors: 0) - a heap climb here tracks purely with job/queue/plugin load, not build workload. Single controller Pod, so no instance filter is needed to disambiguate.

panels.title: Online Agent Nodes
panels.description: Dynamic ci-agent/cd-agent Pods only exist for the lifetime of one build (podRetention: never, see jenkins/jcasc/jenkins.yaml) - a nonzero, non-transient value here for more than a few minutes means an agent Pod failed to clean up.
